english.title: Sexual penetration of a corpse - SOA 2003
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) intentionally performed an act of penetration with

(A)_[a part of your body,]_
(B)_[a thing, namely **(..SPECIFY THE THING..),]_

of a part of the body of a dead person, knowing, or being reckless, as to whether that is what was penetrated and that penetration was sexual
english.legislation: Contrary to section 70 of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: (i) This offence no longer applies after 28th September 2026 due to changes made by the Crime and Policing Act 2026. For the offence applying after this date, see H102803 (no penetration) and H102804 (penetration).(ii) A person convicted of this offence is subject to notification and orders as provided by section 80 of the Act.

other.penalty:
Either waySummary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

(i) On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
(ii) The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
